articles.title: NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: 49ers undefeated no more, as injuries finally too much to overcome in loss to Falcons
articles.summary: The 49ers finally lost after a 6-0 start to the season.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers' injuries finally caught up to them.

The 49ers battled the Atlanta Falcons, which was commendable given their long injury report. But trailing 26-20 late, Brock Purdy threw an interception to linebacker Kendal Daniels. That was it for the 49ers and their undefeated streak to start the season. They are 6-1 after the Falcons won 29-20 .

Losing a road game that was an early start in the Eastern Time Zone isn't a big deal for a team that was 6-0 and up multiple games in the division. Nobody expected the 49ers to go 17-0. The problem isn't a single loss. It's the injuries.

Most other teams dealing with the 49ers' list of injuries would be closer to winless than undefeated. They overcame numerous injuries last season to make the playoffs and then were dealt the same hand this season. Last season and through six games this season, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan found a way to get his team to rise above it.

Sunday brought a new challenge, and that was playing without wide receivers. San Francisco had six receivers either inactive or on injured reserve. Mike Evans is dealing with an Achilles injury and left the team's Week 6 game early due to it. In Week 7 Evans was inactive. That meant Brandin Cooks, who is 33 and hasn't posted a 1,000-yard season since 2021, and Jordan Watkins, who had five career catches before Sunday, started at receiver against the Falcons.

It wasn't just receiver injuries. Defensive end Nick Bosa missed another game. Christian McCaffrey had to manage a thigh injury during the game.

If it was a normal team, even injuries wouldn't be a big deal. Players like Evans and Bosa should be back soon. Every team deals with it. But the 49ers have been the most injured team in the NFL over the past few seasons, and while that seems like terrible luck, it's not turning around. It's also an older team, especially among the elite stars, so more injuries and wearing down over a long season are concerns.

And there's a dropoff to their second team. Without Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and other receivers the 49ers got very little out of their wideouts. With McCaffrey banged up, rookie Kaelon Black fumbled on back-to-back plays, losing the second one. That lost fumble changed the game's momentum.

The 49ers are off to a great start and one loss doesn't change that. They're still in good shape in the NFC West. But it was the first time the 49ers couldn't overcome their injuries. And now they have to hope that, somehow, the bad injury luck doesn't continue.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 7 of the NFL season:

J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo: They each dealt with adversity this season. McCarthy was traded by the Minnesota Vikings and Skattebo found himself deep in the doghouse a week ago.

McCarthy got the start after a hot finish to last week's loss as Jameis Winston's replacement. It was a tough assignment on the road against a good Texans defense, but McCarthy played well. He went 20-of-28 passing for 252 yards.

Skattebo shined too after being practically benched last week. He got no carries against the Saints in Week 6 after fumbling in overtime the week before, but on Sunday he came up with a huge play, a 42-yard run in overtime that got the Giants in field-goal range. They didn't need the field goal as Devin Singletary walked it off with a 30-yard touchdown run for the 27-21 victory. Skattebo had 124 yards rushing and a touchdown.

McCarthy will get more starts going forward after looking good against Houston. And Skattebo is unlikely to be benched again anytime soon.

Harrison Smith and the Vikings' defense: Smith is one of the more popular Minnesota Vikings players in recent years, and he was celebrated as he appeared to retire at the end of last season.

Harrison's retirement didn't last long, as he came back before the season. Then on Sunday he sealed a win with his 40th career interception. The 16-10 win for the Vikings wasn't pretty, and the Indianapolis Colts had a shot to win it at the end on the final drive. But Daniel Jones was pressured and threw downfield, where Smith stepped in front of the receiver for an interception to win the game.

The Vikings are playing great defense this season. They allowed only 218 yards Sunday. After falling behind early they shut out the Colts in the second half. The Vikings are 6-0 and while there are things to correct after Sunday, particularly on offense, it was a good day to cheer for a franchise legend.

Todd Monken: He is getting his first chance to be an NFL head coach at age 60. He's showing that maybe he should have gotten that shot earlier.

The Cleveland Browns are 5-2 and one of the best stories in the NFL. They had another dramatic win Sunday, driving down for a field goal after the Tennessee Titans tied it with 58 seconds left. Andre Szmyt hit the game-winning field goal as time expired and the Browns won 27-24.

Monken took over a situation that seemed terrible due to questions at quarterback. But Deshaun Watson has played well enough, especially with multiple game-winning drives, and the Browns keep winning. That has to be a satisfying start for the rookie head coach.

Aaron Rodgers: He used to typically make a few plays a game with his scrambling ability. That was a long time ago.

Quarterbacks who are creeping up on their 43rd birthday aren't supposed to be effective anymore, unless they're Tom Brady, and they surely shouldn't be scrambling for first downs to clinch wins. But Rodgers' 8-yard scramble on third-and-6 gave the Pittsburgh Steelers a key first down in a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL game in Paris .

More than the play itself, that scramble epitomized how much juice Rodgers still has left in what he has said is his final season. The Steelers are 5-2, putting them in great position to make the playoffs. Rodgers had 212 yards and a touchdown Sunday. While his numbers are a bit down from his fantastic career level, he's still far better than anyone other than Brady has been at his age. If this is it for Rodgers, he's having a good sendoff.

Aaron Glenn: It was questionable that Glenn got a second season coaching the New York Jets, because his first season was terrible. After Sunday, his time with that job seems to be very close to running out.

The Jets lost 28-25 at home to the Miami Dolphins, who were 0-5 coming in. It was a good win for the Dolphins, and the first for Jeff Hafley as an NFL head coach. Miami won't get any 0-17 questions. The Dolphins played like a team that knew it had a shot to beat a poor opponent. And that played out. The Jets didn't play well in any phase. The Jets won their opener against the Titans but have won just once since. The Jets trailed by 11 late, got a touchdown and a two-point conversion, but couldn't stop a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak just inside of the two-minute warning and the Dolphins ran out the rest of the clock for their first win.

The Jets didn't want to fire Glenn after just one season, even though they went 3-14 and there were some alarming signs from Glenn. Glenn replaced most of his staff over the offseason. The results are the same. An embarrassing loss on Sunday is a terrible development for Glenn, who might not make it to the end of the season as Jets head coach. It's possible he won't make it to Week 8.

The second half Ravens: The Baltimore Ravens need to figure out how to play better after halftime. Because it has cost them three wins already this season.

The Ravens, whose first two losses came after leading 14-6 and 10-0 at halftime, led the Cincinnati Bengals 13-0 after the first half Sunday in a big AFC North showdown. Then the offense, without Lamar Jackson, stopped moving the ball. And the defense, which had pressured Joe Burrow often in the first half, got run off the field in the second half. Burrow had 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half alone and the Ravens won 35-13 with five unanswered touchdowns in the second half. You can't blame Jackson's absence for that. The Bengals trailed by 13 at halftime but blew the Ravens out so bad in the second half that they pulled Burrow for the final few minutes.

The Ravens will be division contenders again after Jackson returns. But there's frustration growing with why he was out again with an ankle injury, and there's plenty of other issues that are now nagging at the Ravens.

The weird NFC South: The one team that looked like it could be a decent team out of the NFC South trailed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who had just one win, 33-6 at halftime. At home.

The Carolina Panthers' momentum hit a wall on Sunday. The Buccaneers, 1-5 coming into Sunday's game, blew out Carolina 43-13. It got ugly early. A strip-sack on Bryce Young, who had been playing very well before Sunday, was returned by the Bucs for a touchdown (with a flip into the end zone from 280-pound Calijah Kancey) and a 17-0 lead. Bryce Young had just 163 yards, two interceptions and a lost fumble. When the Panthers finally scored, their extra point was blocked and returned by Tampa Bay for two points. The Panthers played a sloppy game on offense, defense and special teams. Baker Mayfield was back but the Buccaneers hardly needed him. Mayfield had just 64 yards passing but the Panthers were imploding on the other side of the field.

It's hard to say a 2-5 team is back in a division race, but it's not like the NFC South has any good teams, it appears. That's nothing new.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Wins 1st Giants Start, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Skattebo, Stroud, Top Players
articles.summary: Let the J.J. McCarthy era begin for the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Let the J.J. McCarthy era begin for the New York Giants.

McCarthy led the Giants to a 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday at Reliant Stadium in his first start with the team. New York is now 4-2-1, while the disappointing Texans fell to 2-5 on the campaign.

While McCarthy was largely excellent, it was the rushing attack that won it in overtime. Cam Skattebo broke through for a 42-yard run, while Devin Singletary finished it with a 30-yard touchdown.

It was a stunning result and a credit to Skattebo in particular, who bounced back from zero carries in his last game to thrive in this one.

All eyes were on McCarthy coming into his first start with the Giants since they acquired him via trade from a Minnesota Vikings team that gave up on him early after using the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft on the Michigan product.

McCarthy earned the start by playing well in place of Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter of New York's loss to the New Orleans Saints and looked comfortable early against Houston by hitting Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields for long gains and directing a touchdown drive that Tyrone Tracy Jr. capped off in the end zone.

That was just the start of his first half, as he found Thomas Fidone II for another deep completion that set up a Winston score on a tush push.

McCarthy's Giants would have finished the first half with even more points if Dominic Zvada didn't miss two field goals, and the Texans entered intermission with all the momentum as a result after Stroud tied the game by hitting Tank Dell for 43 yards, Marvin Harrison Jr. for a touchdown and Cade Stover for the two-point conversion.

Dell's catch in particular fired up the crowd, as Sunday was his first game since he suffered a significant knee injury in December 2024.

Yet for as thrilling as the first half was for the two offenses, the exact opposite played out as the sides traded four straight punts in the third quarter.

It was a notable development for Houston's defense, which was expected to be among the league's best coming into the season but has largely underperformed to this point. The windows that were initially there for McCarthy started to disappear, although a fake tush push led to a long run for Skattebo to give the Giants some momentum.

It was just the start for the physical running back, who exploded through multiple Houston defenders for a 16-yard touchdown run to give the Giants the lead with fewer than nine minutes remaining.

Skattebo's efforts gave New York's defense the chance to win it, but Stroud responded with a touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson to force overtime.

However, New York took advantage of the extra period and now heads into the bye week with plenty of momentum. As for the Texans, they are also going into their bye week but will look to turn things around after a disappointing result.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 7 Results, Who Could Chargers & Dolphins Take?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are now the lone winless team in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are now the lone winless team in the NFL.

The Miami Dolphins' win over the New York Jets put the Chargers removed them from the winless ranks.

Miami is still inside the top three of the projected 2027 NFL draft order alongside the Chargers and the Tennessee Titans.

The Chargers will be the No. 1 pick in the projected draft order after Week 7 because they are on a bye. There's no clear end in sight to the losing run, though, since they come out of the off week to play the Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens.

The Chargers, Titans, Dolphins, Washington Commanders and Texans are currently the top five teams in the projected draft order.

6. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 2-5)

The longer the Chargers stay first in the projected order, the better the chances are for Jeremiah Smith to be the No. 1 overall pick.

The Chargers would be more likely to get rid of their offensive coaches, or even Jim Harbaugh, then they would Justin Herbert because of the money attached to the franchise quarterback.

Smith is currently second in the FBS in receiving yards and second in receiving touchdowns. He's averaging 18.9 yards per catch this season and has averaged 17 yards per catch in every Ohio State game this season.

Smith would be the obvious choice for the Chargers because he would provide a huge boost to the team's offense. He'd be an instant upgrade over Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston.

The Ohio State wide receiver would also be a huge upgrade for the Dolphins and the Titans, but those teams might be more invested in the quarterback market.

If Miami wants to hold on to Malik Willis, or if it doesn't believe in the quarterback class, it could go the Smith route as well. The same goes for the Titans depending on what happens with Cam Ward.

Arch Manning's draft stock has been on a rollercoaster throughout the Texas Longhorns' season.

Manning bounced back a bit on Saturday with 212 passing yards and a touchdown pass in the win over the Ole Miss Rebels.

Manning did throw a pair of interceptions in the win, so he wasn't perfect by any stretch of the imagination.

However, the Texas quarterback did play better than he did in the losses to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators.

The quarterback class as a whole hasn't performed well during the 2026 college football regular season, Manning included.

Manning has a handful of high-profile SEC games left to play, so if he plays better, he could boost his draft stock.

Miami, Tennessee and others should at least look at Manning throughout the rest of the college football season, but right now, there's no guarantee he'll be in the mix to be the top signal-caller chosen.

articles.title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to 2nd-half collapse vs. Bengals
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens appeared to be on their way to another surprising win with Tyler Huntley at the helm of their offense, taking a 13-0 lead into halftime...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens appeared to be on their way to another surprising win with Tyler Huntley at the helm of their offense, taking a 13-0 lead into halftime against the Cincinnati Bengals.

But Baltimore's defense completely folded in the second half with no support from an offense that managed just two first downs after their first drive on the third quarter. The Bengals dropped 35 unanswered points, leading to a dismal 35-13 final result that leaves the Ravens at 4-3 heading into a tough stretch with two games against division-leading teams in the next 11 days. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's instant reactions to Sunday's loss:

Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver should have to watch that second half before every single one of their defensive meetings for the rest of the season. Allowing four straight touchdown drives out of halftime – three of at least 65 yards – is completely inexcusable for what is supposed to be one of the better defenses in the NFL. On every play, the Ravens seemed to be a second behind, unable to finish plays in the backfield or limit explosive passes over the top. Those struggles distracted from another woeful second half from an offense that simple cannot get out of its own way with procedural penalties. Vega Ioane's knee injury also seemed to have a major impact with a steep drop-off in right guard play to Emery Jones. But regardless of his personnel issues, Declan Doyle's inability to figure out short yardage is maddening. Even when Lamar Jackson is back, this team has major issues that currently will keep them far from the AFC North crown.

I'm not really sure where you go from here if you're the Ravens. I don't know if the stats would support this but this must be one of the more stark performance differences between a second half and first half in NFL history. The Ravens completely dominated the first half – but it didn't matter. Predictably, they fell apart the moment the second half started allowing the Bengals to score touchdowns on every drive. Offensively, the Ravens couldn't do much in the second half and couldn't convert in short yardage or in the red zone – even when the offense was productive. Even if Lamar Jackson comes back healthy, there's no way to have optimism about them. The offensive line can't hold a block, the defense can't tackle, and the pass rush completely disappeared in the second half. This looks like the same team from last year that's been covered up by an easy schedule. It might be an overreaction, but Jesse Minter and Eric DeCosta's seats should be warming up a little.

The fanbase used to be angry about this. Then they became numb. Now, I think we might all actually be expecting the blown leads.

I'm grateful that Lamar is expected back next week, but he's going to need to put on a master class if they have any hope of keeping pace in the next couple of games. I don't know what the plan was in the second half on defense, but the absences of Tavius Robinson, Jaylinn Hawkins and Roquan Smith (for a potion of the half) should never have had an impact like that. To have an opponent score touchdowns on five straight possessions is inexcusable. Back-to-back weeks of getting humiliated on defense by division opponents has this defense looking mentally broken, and I'm not sure how they fix it.

The Ravens being this helpless without Lamar Jackson is not a good sign for this team going forward. I truly do not understand how the defense could allow 35 points in the second half after shutting the Bengals out through the first two quarters. Missed tackles, blown coverages, and a lack of finishing sacks has haunted this unit for years now and I am completely lost on how Jesse Minter is supposed to go about fixing it. Giving up plays to a talented Cincinnati offense was always expected, but 35 points in one half is simply inexcusable with the resources invested into the defense and a highly-touted defensive head coach now. On offense, I would love to say that the issues boiled down to Jackson's absence, but the problems go beyond just quarterback play. The offensive line continues to be a revolving door due to injuries, with Vega Ioane being the latest, while Short-yardage situations feel impossibly hard. Derrick Henry, when not getting hit behind the line of scrimmage, has not looked like usual dominant self outside of a few games this season. Declan Doyle needs to seriously consider giving another running back the ball on short-yardage runs going forward. Getting Jackson back next week will help tremendously, but Minter, Doyle, Anthony Weaver, and Anthony Levine Sr. all have some serious soul searching to do after these past two losses.

The Ravens are a bad team right now. The roster needs a massive reset. Lamar Jackson doesn't add enough to fix what happened here. The offensive line is too soft to get a yard when it's 3rd/4th-and-short, and losing Vega Ioane isn't enough to take the entire blame there. The scripted plays and drives on offense were great again, but Huntley once again couldn't do much outside of that and they didn't convert in the red zone enough. The defense pissed down their leg in the second half once more, giving up 35 unanswered.

I'm over blaming coaches. We blamed Harbaugh and Orr and Monken and Roman and Macdonald (early in his career). Now everybody wants to be mad at Minter and Doyle. But I'm over it.

They are mentally and physically soft. Minter and Doyle aren't perfect. But eventually players need to be held accountable.

articles.title: Ranking the worst losses in an upset-filled Week 7 in the NFL, from Panthers flop to Jets disaster
articles.summary: The Panthers and Jets were among the teams who will regret Sunday's results.
articles.body:
At this point in the NFL season, there has been separation between the contenders who are looking for a playoff spot and the pretenders whose seasons are almost over. That means, though, that upset losses are getting even more devastating.

In Week 7 in particular, several of the league's worst teams gave their opponents all they could in search of a rare win. In some cases, those teams actually pulled off the upset, handing the other team a loss that they will regret for the rest of the year.

Whether it was the Miami Dolphins picking up their first win of the season ot the Carolina Panthers no-showing at home, some of this week's results produced losses that frustrated many fans across the country.

Here's a look at the worst losses from the early window in Week 7.

5. 49ers undefeated season ends in Atlanta

The San Francisco 49ers looked like the best team in the NFL through the first six weeks, but they finally dropped a game against the Atlanta Falcons . Injuries and inconsistencies on Sunday led to the 49ers' struggles in an early kickoff on the road, making it so there is now one less undefeated team.

All things considered, this loss isn't too bad for the 49ers. It was on the road on the East Coast, which in and of itself is not an easy task for West Coast teams, and the Falcons have shown some serious fight after a tough 0-2 start.

Additionally, this loss is not in the division, which should give Atlanta a little bit of solace heading home.

4. Texans falter against Giants QB J.J. McCarthy

The Houston Texans put themselves in a major hole by starting the season 0-4, making every game the rest of the way crucial. While they won the last two games to get back on track, the Texans went one step backwards with a home loss to the New York Giants .

The Giants were starting J.J. McCarthy for the first time this year, presenting the Texans' defense a chance to flex its muscles. Instead, McCarthy had a nice day through the air, outgaining C.J. Stroud with 99 more passing yards.

Houston's defense allowed 400 yards to a Giants offense on its third quarterback this season, while the Texans' offense produced just 237 yards on the day. Overall, it was a humbling loss for a Texans team that now falls to 2-5.

3. Ravens fade vs. Bengals without Lamar

The Baltimore Ravens began Sunday strong as they held the Cincinnati Bengals scoreless in the first half, taking a 13-0 lead into the break. In the second half, though, the Ravens completely fell apart, letting the Bengals score 35 unanswered points as the Bengals won in a blowout.

Losing without Lamar Jackson is not necessarily surprising, but the way the Ravens lost was certainly disconcerting. Baltimore was home against a division rival, in a very competitive division, and now sits alone in last place in the AFC North.

The Ravens are now 0-2 in division games with back-to-back losses to the Browns and Bengals. While Cincinnati is on the upswing following the win, the Ravens need Jackson to hit the ground running when he returns.

2. Jets suffer inexcusable loss to winless Dolphins

It's not often that the New York Jets are the better team in a game, and they were on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. That didn't matter, though, when the Dolphins got their first win of the season on the road against the Jets.

The loss means head coach Aaron Glenn is now 0-8 against AFC East teams since he took over as Jets head coach, along with a 5-19 record overall. This is the kind of loss that could cost Glenn his job at one point, even if that doesn't happen midseason.

Jets fans had hopes that their team could actually compete for a playoff spot this year. Instead, New York is 2-5 and faces another lost season.

1. Panthers flop in blowout loss against Buccaneers

The Carolina Panthers had a chance to bury their division rival, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and take full control in the NFC South. Instead, the Panthers laid an egg while Baker Mayfield's return to the lineup led to the Buccaneers' second win of the season.

Carolina had hopes this year to take a step forward, with this being the type of game that contenders use to make their mark. However, all three phases of the Panthers failed on Sunday, highlighted by allowing 26 points in the second quarter alone.

Now, the Panthers not only let the Buccaneers back into the division race, but they also ceded space with the Falcons atop the standings. Carolina went from firm control of the division to barely hanging on.

articles.title: Where Titans land after loss vs Browns for NFL draft order
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are in the race to get the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft after Week 7.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans went back to their losing ways Oct. 25 with a last-second, 27-24 home defeat against the Cleveland Browns, moving them up to second in the standings for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

A week after their first win of the season, 26-20 against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 18, the Titans fell to 1-6 and moved from third to second in terms of where they currently are in the NFL draft order, per tankathon . The Titans last held the No. 1 pick in 2025.

According to tankathon.com , the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6), who did not play this week, would have the top pick based on their strength of schedule, which is the weakest among the worst teams in the NFL. The Miami Dolphins (1-5) picked up their first win of the season Oct. 25 against the Jets, but their strength of schedule is better than the Titans'.

Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos

Tennessee chose quarterback Cam Ward out of Miami with the first pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

Here's the updated first-round order for the 2027 NFL Draft as Week 7 results come in. The draft order is according to Tankathon , which calculates strength of schedule differently from the NFL:

LA Chargers (0-6) .538 strength of schedule

Cleveland Browns (via Rams) (2-4) .524 SOS

Dallas Cowboys (via Packers) (4-2) .519 SOS

NFL Draft order is decided by the reverse order of each team's finish in the regular season and postseason.

The team with the worst record gets the No. 1 pick. Every pick after that, through pick 20, is determined by regular-season records from worst to best.

Should teams have identical records, the first tiebreaker is strength of schedule, meaning the team whose opponents had the worst combined winning % receives the higher pick.

If that number is identical, the second tiebreaker is division/conference, meaning head-to-head games, common opponents, strength of victory.

The final tiebreaker, should the first two not work, is a coin toss.

That doesn't seem likely, but with 10 games remaining, the Titans will learn more about Cam Ward.

Side note: Five of Mel Kiper's top 10 prospects for the 2027 draft are quarterbacks, though Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith tops the list.

Would the Titans opt for a receiver with top pick?

Taking a receiver and giving Ward some ,more tools with which to work would make sense. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, considered the best receiver prospect who is draft eligible, could help in Ward's development.

Would the Titans trade the first pick in the NFL Draft?

If stacking talent is the plan, trading the pick for players and/or more picks could speed up the Titans' rebuilding process.

Teams have traded first pick in the NFL Draft 13 times since 1967, when the common draft era began.

The Titans/Oilers have had the first overall pick in the NFL Draft three times.

Would the Titans draft Arch Manning with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft?

While another quarterback named Manning playing for a football team in Tennessee would be cute for a movie script, the reality is, Texas quarterback Arch Manning, nephew of former Tennessee Vols quarterback Peyton Manning, has done nothing to prove himself worthy of being the top overall pick.
